findings.evidence: The "project-archived" state's only control is "Back to your projects" (project-archived-exit-link, targeting #workspace-overview); no control in this state, and no link anywhere else in the artifact, targets a restore or unarchive action.
findings.fix: Add a restore or unarchive control, reachable either from the project-archived state or from an archived-projects list, that returns the project to the active list.
findings.violation: Archiving is reasonably reversible in this product (an "active projects list" implies a corresponding archived list a team could restore from), but the artifact treats it as permanent: once archive-confirm's Archive control commits, no state the artifact defines offers a way back.

findings.evidence: carries no "required" attribute, and the control that actually advances the flow, Continue, is a plain link rather than the form's own submit control, so nothing in the artifact ties reaching invite-sent to the field holding a value at all.
findings.fix: Make the field required and route Continue through the form's own submit action (or an equivalent validation step) so an empty or malformed address blocks the transition to invite-sent instead of reaching it silently.
findings.location: the "invite-member" section, the email input (invite-member-email-input) and the Continue link (invite-member-continue-link)
findings.violation: Nothing constrains or checks the email field before the flow proceeds to "Invite sent": a user can leave the field empty or malformed and still reach a confirmation state that reports success, so the likely error of an unfilled or mistyped address is never caught anywhere in the artifact.

findings.evidence: "Import failed. Error code IMP-500. Contact support if this continues."
findings.fix: Replace or supplement the code with plain language naming what failed (for example, which file or which step of the import) and why, in terms the user recognizes.
findings.violation: The message reports only that the import failed and surfaces a raw internal error code, with nothing naming which file, project, or step caused the failure, so the user cannot tell what about their own action or data was at fault.

findings.evidence: The only control in "import-status" is "Back to your projects" (import-status-exit-link, targeting #workspace-overview); no control anywhere in the artifact retries or resumes the import, and workspace-overview defines no import-trigger control either.
findings.fix: Add a retry control to the import-status state, or, if import is triggered elsewhere, ensure that control is defined and reachable from this error state.
findings.violation: The error state names no recovery action the user can take from where they are standing: there is no retry control at the error itself, and no import-triggering control exists anywhere else in the artifact for the user to fall back to.

findings.evidence: Each form's <button type="submit">Save</button> sits in a <form> with no action attribute, and no section the artifact defines represents a post-save state, message, or changed control; the page the user is already on specifies no visible change after Save is used.
findings.fix: For each Save control, specify what the user sees immediately after: a success message, a changed field state, or a defined next state, placed where the user is already looking.

instances.evidence: <button type="submit">Save</button> in a <form> with no action attribute and no defined post-save state or message

findings.location: the "project-settings" section, the Save button (project-settings-save-btn); the "invite-member" section, the Save button (invite-member-save-btn); the "notification-settings" section, the Save button (notification-settings-save-btn)
findings.violation: Three state-changing Save actions are specified with no visible indication of what the system did or whether it succeeded, so a user who clicks Save has no way to tell from the artifact whether the change took effect.

findings.evidence: <button type="button" aria-label="Duplicate project"></button> has no href, no form association, and appears in no edge of the artifact's state graph; no section or message anywhere in the artifact reflects a duplicated project.
findings.fix: Specify what happens immediately after Duplicate is used, such as a new entry appearing in the projects list on workspace-overview or a confirmation message naming the new project.
findings.location: the "project-settings" section, the icon-only "Duplicate project" button (project-settings-duplicate-btn)
findings.violation: Duplicating a project is a state-changing action (it would create a new project) specified with zero visible indication of outcome: no new list entry, no confirmation, no defined next state.

findings.evidence: The "invite-sent" state's only copy is "An invite was sent to the address entered above," and defines no element that redisplays the actual email address entered on the prior invite-member screen.
findings.fix: Display the entered email address directly in the invite-sent confirmation text instead of referring back to the prior screen.
findings.violation: The confirmation refers to a value from the previous state ("the address entered above") without repeating it, so a user who wants to verify which address received the invite must recall it or navigate back rather than read it at the point of confirmation.
